name_story.story: Aisyah can be understood through the Arabic form عَائِشَة, whose central sense is aisyah; living, prosperous (indonesian form). Aisyah is the Indonesian/Malay form of Arabic عَائِشَة (ʿĀʾisha), associated with the sense 'living, prosperous'. It was borne by the Prophet's wife.

faq.a: Aisyah is associated with the Arabic form عَائِشَة, whose core sense is aisyah; living, prosperous (indonesian form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Aisyah?
faq.a: Aisyah is associated with Arabic. Aisyah is the Indonesian/Malay form of Arabic عَائِشَة (ʿĀʾisha), associated with the sense 'living, prosperous'. It was borne by the Prophet's wife.
Yes — the underlying form عَائِشَة is Arabic.
Aisyah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aisyah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿĀʾisha is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Aisyah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aisyah is rendered عائشہ and carries the sense عائشہ، زندہ.

faq.q: What does Aisyah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aisyah is rendered عایشه and carries the sense عایشه، زنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ai-syah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aisyah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aisyah, aisyah. Script forms are عائشہ, عايشه, عایشه, عَائِشَة, आइशा.

faq.q: Is Aisyah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
